description: Minimal Clojure protocol model across three namespaces: two defprotocols, records and a deftype that satisfy them inline, an extend-type, an extend-protocol (whose direction is INVERTED relative to extend-type), and a (:gen-class) directive. Exercises namespace/type extraction and namespace->type CONTAINS, and — the reason the fixture exists (#6370) — the protocol-satisfaction relation, including the depth-1 token shape that separates a supertype from a symbol in a method body, and the two places a declaration can be written without meaning it.

expected_entities.name: app.protocols
expected_entities.note: namespace component; the anchor a (:gen-class) edge would use if this file had one.

expected_entities.name: Shape
expected_entities.note: defprotocol carrying a docstring; the root three types conform to.

expected_entities.name: Sized
expected_entities.note: defprotocol whose tail carries the option pair `:extend-via-metadata true` — a bare depth-1 symbol that must not be read as a supertype.

expected_entities.name: Circle
expected_entities.note: defrecord satisfying two protocols and one JVM nested-class interface inline, alternating symbol/list.

expected_entities.name: Square
expected_entities.note: deftype; its method body contains a `let` whose bindings are bare symbols.

expected_entities.name: Plain
expected_entities.note: defrecord with a field vector and NO protocol — the negative control.

expected_entities.name: compute-area
expected_entities.note: A plain defn. It is named inside two method bodies, which is what makes the depth fence's forbidden rows resolvable to a real entity rather than to a bare string.

expected_entities.name: app.extend
expected_entities.note: namespace component; owner of the (:gen-class) edges.

expected_entities.name: Triangle
expected_entities.note: extended by extend-type — the subject is the HEAD symbol.

expected_entities.name: Hexagon
expected_entities.note: extended by extend-protocol — the subject is a TAIL symbol.

expected_entities.name: Weighted
expected_entities.note: defprotocol declared in the SAME file as the extend-protocol form that names it. That co-location is what makes the direction forbidden row reachable — see its note.

expected_relationships.note: #6370: the FIRST depth-1 symbol of a defrecord tail, reached across the field vector. A producer that took the token immediately after the name would bind `[radius]` and fail this.

#6370: the SECOND depth-1 symbol of the same tail, reached across an intervening method list. This is the only row in the fixture that grades the alternation — a producer that stopped at the first supertype passes the row above and fails this one.

#6370: the THIRD depth-1 symbol of Circle's tail is `java.util.Map$Entry`, JVM nested-class notation. Two facts stated rather than implied: the target charset must admit `$` or the token is rejected WHOLE by an anchored regex and the edge simply never exists (a silent recall miss, which is what the first draft of this extractor did); and resolution then collapses the unindexed dotted target onto a top-segment SCOPE.External node, the same pre-existing behaviour the two (:gen-class) rows below describe. The row is distinguishable from those two by its FROM endpoint.
#6370: owner keyword `deftype` rather than `defrecord`. This row varies the DECLARATION KEYWORD and holds the tail shape constant, so a producer hard-coded to defrecord keeps Circle and loses this.
#6370: `(extend-type Triangle Shape ...)`. The head symbol is the IMPLEMENTER here.

#6370: `(extend-protocol Sized Hexagon ...)`. The head symbol is the PROTOCOL here — the inverse of the row above, on a form of identical shape. This is the only expected row that fails when the two keywords share one code path, and it fails while the EDGE COUNT is unchanged: the swapped edge is Sized -> Hexagon, which is this fixture's forbidden row of the same name.

#6370: `(:gen-class :extends java.util.AbstractList)` — the ONLY construct in Clojure that names a real superclass, and the only EXTENDS this extractor emits. Two facts about the target are stated rather than implied: the written form is `java.util.AbstractList`, and resolution collapses an unindexed dotted target onto a top-segment SCOPE.External node (`java`), which is pre-existing resolver behaviour for dotted targets and not something #6370 changed. So this row grades the LADDER ARM, not target precision — which is what it is here for, since it is the only row whose Kind is EXTENDS.

#6370: `(:gen-class :implements [java.lang.Runnable java.io.Closeable])`. Same owner and same resolved target as the row above, differing ONLY in Kind — which is precisely what makes the pair grade the keyword-to-kind mapping: an arm that emitted EXTENDS for both, or IMPLEMENTS for both, keeps one row and loses the other.

#6370: a SECOND extend-protocol, this one naming a protocol declared in the same file. Its purpose is the forbidden row Weighted -> Triangle: the swapped edge can only be OBSERVED when the protocol has a component in the file the extend-protocol form lives in, and Sized does not (it is declared in protocols.clj), so the Hexagon/Sized pair alone leaves the swap visible as a MISS and not as a false positive.

Pre-existing clojure behaviour, held so the fixture measures more than the one edge kind #6370 adds — and so a regression that dropped ALL embedded relationships is distinguishable from one that dropped only IMPLEMENTS.
Pre-existing clojure behaviour in a second namespace, on the type that is a conformance TARGET rather than a conforming type.

forbidden_relationships.note: #6370 OVER-FIRING, depth fence: `(area [_] (compute-area radius))` calls compute-area at paren-depth 2. FIRES, verified: replacing `if depth == 1` with `if depth >= 1` in depth1Symbols makes the gate report this hit.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, depth fence via a `let` BINDING VALUE rather than a call head: `(let [helper compute-area edge side] ...)`. FIRES under the same mutant. Two rows rather than one because a producer that skipped only list HEADS would keep this one.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, the field vector: `radius` is a FIELD, not a supertype. It is inside `[...]`, so the same depth test excludes it. FIRES under the same mutant, and it is the row that shows the field vector is skipped BY SHAPE and not by a position rule.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, `(comment ...)`: an indented `(defrecord Scratch [z] Ghost ...)` inside a rich-comment block. Its ENTITY is extracted today (deftypeRE's `^\s*\(` allows leading whitespace) and this fixture does NOT forbid the entity, because that over-fire is pre-existing and outside this change. What is forbidden is the EDGE. FIRES, verified: deleting the blankCommentForms call from scanClojureHierarchy makes the gate report this hit.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, string content: the same declaration written inside a multi-line string. Same split as the row above — entity pre-existing, edge forbidden. FIRES, verified: deleting the stripStringsAndComments call makes the gate report this hit. Two separate rows because the two sanitisers are independent and a mutant of either leaves the other's row clean, which is how they are shown NOT to mask each other.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, direction — the headline trap of this change. `(extend-protocol Weighted Triangle ...)` states that Triangle implements Weighted, not the reverse; extend-type spells the SAME shape the other way round, so one shared code path emits every extend-protocol edge backwards. FIRES, verified: routing extend-protocol through the extend-type arm produces exactly this edge, and the gate reports it as 1 forbidden hit.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, direction, the CROSS-FILE case. NOT FIRED by the swap mutant, stated plainly rather than implied: Sized is declared in protocols.clj while the extend-protocol form is in extend.clj, and an extend-* edge anchors only on a component THIS FILE declares (see the hierarchy.go header), so the swapped edge is dropped for want of an anchor and shows up as a MISSING Hexagon -> Sized instead. The same-file version of this hazard is the Weighted -> Triangle row above, which does fire. Kept as an absence fence for a producer that anchors extend-* edges by bare name across files.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, leading `$`: the target charset admits `$` INSIDE a name (java.util.Map$Entry, on Circle above) but not at the START of one — `Map$Entry` is a type, `$Bogus` is not. The two positions are separate guards and the Map$Entry row grades only the first. The bad token sits beside a good one (`Shape`, whose edge is a must-have row) so the rejection is graded per TOKEN, not per form. FIRES, verified: widening the regex's leading class from `[A-Za-z_]` to `[A-Za-z_$]` makes the gate report this hit.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, defprotocol option value: `(defprotocol Sized :extend-via-metadata true (size [this]))` puts the bare symbol `true` at depth 1. It is not a supertype, and defprotocol is excluded from the scanned keywords at the call site for exactly this reason. FIRES, verified: adding `defprotocol` to clojureHierarchyHeadRE AND to the defrecord/deftype switch arm — both edits are needed, since the regex alone matches a keyword no arm handles — makes the gate report this hit.

#6370 OVER-FIRING: Plain declares no protocol at all. NOT FIRED by any mutant tried, stated plainly rather than implied — the depth mutant binds Plain to nothing, because Plain's only depth-1 token is its field vector `[x]` and `x` is not a name any other row uses. This is an absence FENCE for a producer that defaults a protocol-less record to a root, a shape no single edit of this extractor produces.
